title: Tailspin Toys — Identity, secrets & governance hardening
scenario:
Tailspin Toys runs production workloads in a single Azure subscription and a Microsoft Entra tenant shared with its M365 estate. The security team has set these requirements:

1. Administrators must hold no standing Owner or Global Administrator rights. They must be able to request time-bound elevation, gated by manager approval and MFA, for a maximum of 4 hours, with a full audit trail.
2. A nightly invoicing daemon (no signed-in user) must be able to read all mailboxes via Microsoft Graph; access must be reviewed and cannot silently expand without admin visibility.
3. An automated deployment pipeline running on an Azure VM must retrieve a database connection string from Key Vault without any client secret stored on the VM or in code.
4. A new Key Vault must default to a centrally governed, granular access model without vault access policies, with public network access disabled and a private endpoint.
5. Every newly created resource must carry a mandatory 'DataClassification' tag before it can be provisioned, enforced automatically rather than relying on manual discipline.
6. Backups of the finance database must be protected so that even a compromised administrator account cannot delete or shorten their retention during the retention period.

title: Woodgrove Bank — Storage, database & network segmentation
scenario:
Woodgrove Bank is preparing its Azure estate for a financial-services security audit. Requirements:

1. A storage account holding scanned customer documents must reject anonymous container access and plaintext HTTP, and must never authorize access with the account's master key.
2. A backup archive storage account must be reachable only from a specific on-premises network connected via ExpressRoute, with zero public internet exposure.
3. National ID numbers stored in an Azure SQL column must remain unreadable in plaintext even to the database administrators, while still being queryable by the application.
4. The compliance team must be able to review a full, immutable history of every login and query made against the customer-accounts table.
5. All egress traffic from the 'core-banking' subnet must be inspected by a centrally managed, reusable firewall policy shared across two regional secured hubs.
6. Central security must be able to enforce a tenant-wide rule blocking a known-malicious IP range across all 40 VNets, without editing each VNet's NSGs individually and without resource owners being able to override it.
7. A public-facing loan-application web app must be protected against SQL injection and cross-site scripting at a global edge point of presence, since customers connect from multiple continents.

title: Litware Inc. — Compute, containers & AI workload rollout
scenario:
Litware Inc. is rolling out Microsoft 365 Copilot and a custom Foundry-based support agent alongside its existing Azure compute estate. Requirements:

1. Before enabling Copilot tenant-wide, the security team must find SharePoint sites shared far too broadly (e.g. 'everyone except external') so Copilot cannot surface that content to the wrong users.
2. The new support agent, built in Microsoft Foundry, must have a governed, first-class identity so Conditional Access and risk-based policies can apply to it just like a human user.
3. The agent must be blocked automatically if Microsoft Entra flags it as high-risk, without requiring a human to notice first.
4. Model endpoints behind the support agent must enforce Microsoft Entra authentication instead of API keys, and apply token-based rate limits to defend against cost-abuse ('wallet') attacks.
5. Administrators must RDP into a small fleet of management VMs without any of them ever having a public IP address, and only after an explicit, time-scoped request.
6. A containerized order-processing workload on AKS must authenticate cluster users with their corporate identities rather than static kubeconfig credentials, and must pull images from a registry with no anonymous access.
7. A public order-status API must validate Microsoft Entra tokens and apply per-client rate limits, fronted privately rather than exposing the backend directly.

title: Relecloud — Multicloud posture, detection & response
scenario:
Relecloud is centralizing security posture and operations across a growing multicloud estate (Azure, one AWS account, one GCP project). Requirements:

1. The security team needs one score summarizing configuration compliance across all three clouds in a single place, prioritized by impact.
2. Before onboarding a newly acquired subsidiary, the team wants to discover the subsidiary's internet-facing web servers the way an external attacker would see them.
3. VMs across the estate must be scanned for known vulnerabilities and malware without installing any agent on them.
4. The SOC wants incidents automatically created when suspicious Microsoft Entra sign-in patterns are detected, correlated across multiple log sources, and investigated with a single hunting query language.
5. A firewall appliance in a branch office must forward its logs into the same central platform used for the cloud logs above.
6. A Logic App must automatically open a ticket the moment Microsoft Defender for Cloud raises a high-severity alert — independent of whether a Sentinel incident is also created.
7. Analysts should be able to ask, in natural language, 'summarize this incident and tell me what this KQL query does' from inside the existing investigation portal, without switching tools.
8. Logs required for a 7-year regulatory retention obligation, but queried only a few times a year, must be stored as cheaply as possible.

title: Goal: just-in-time, approval-gated elevation
scenario: Goal: Ensure administrators hold no standing Owner or Global Administrator rights, and can only obtain them after MFA and manager approval, for a maximum of 4 hours, with a full audit trail of every activation.

title: Goal: tenant-wide consent, not per-app secrets
scenario: Goal: A background job must read mailbox data via Microsoft Graph with no signed-in user, and any grant of that permission must be visible and reviewable by administrators, not silently expandable by end users.

title: Goal: credential-free access to Key Vault
scenario: Goal: A deployment pipeline running on an Azure VM must read a secret from Key Vault. No client secret or connection string may ever be stored on the VM or in source code.

title: Goal: automatic tagging with no manual step
scenario: Goal: Every newly created resource must carry a 'DataClassification' tag the moment it is provisioned, with zero reliance on the person creating it remembering to add it.

title: Goal: no anonymous access, no master-key exposure
scenario: Goal: A storage account holding scanned documents must never allow anonymous container access, and no client should ever authenticate using the account's master key.

title: Goal: unreadable-even-to-DBAs column encryption
scenario: Goal: A column of national ID numbers in Azure SQL must remain unreadable in plaintext to database administrators, while the application can still query it normally.

title: Goal: centralized, override-proof network block
scenario: Goal: Block a known-malicious IP range from reaching any of 40 VNets tenant-wide, enforced centrally, so that no individual resource owner's NSG can override the block.

title: Goal: find oversharing before Copilot amplifies it
scenario: Goal: Before enabling Microsoft 365 Copilot tenant-wide, discover SharePoint sites that are shared far more broadly than intended, so Copilot cannot surface that content to the wrong users.

title: Goal: zero standing exposure for VM management
scenario: Goal: Administrators must be able to RDP into management VMs, but the VMs must never have a public IP and the management port must stay closed until an explicit, time-scoped request is approved.

title: Goal: registry with zero anonymous pull
scenario: Goal: A container registry feeding a production AKS cluster must have zero anonymous pull access and must authenticate every client via Microsoft Entra identity rather than a shared admin password.

title: Goal: one prioritized score across three clouds
scenario: Goal: Produce a single, impact-prioritized posture score covering Azure, one AWS account, and one GCP project, without deploying agents everywhere first.

title: Goal: correlated, cross-source incident creation
scenario: Goal: Automatically create a single incident when a suspicious Microsoft Entra sign-in pattern is detected, correlating signals from multiple log sources into one investigation.

title: Goal: natural-language investigation, no tool-switching
scenario: Goal: Let an analyst ask, in natural language, for an incident summary and an explanation of a KQL query, from directly inside the existing investigation portal.
